tb21_profile.skill: Bounded-concurrency asyncio with correct cancellation semantics: a semaphore that never leaks a permit, CancelledError propagated so every task's finally block runs, KeyboardInterrupt handled without hanging or orphaning tasks
tb21_profile.domain: Python asyncio — Semaphore, gather/TaskGroup, Task.cancel, CancelledError, signal handling in the event loop
tb21_profile.task_form: implement-from-spec: one function at a fixed path and signature, judged by adversarial tests that cancel mid-flight and assert cleanup ran

verifier_notes: No grade I disagreed with, but two relevance notes. Terminal-Lego's asyncio block is the most on-topic text in the whole pool (task_10192 cleans up an event loop after KeyboardInterrupt, task_10167 is a semaphore concurrency limiter) yet its verifiers are thin: task_10192 has 15 tests of which exactly one pins a value, and task_15145 is 1 substantive out of 28. They are honest per_source entries and I kept them out of final_top10 for that reason, not because of the hard rule. Among TerminalWorld picks tw_196065 (bounded parallel command runner) and tw_534776 (clean exit on SIGINT) are FREE and per_source only; they are still the two most relevant things TerminalWorld has.

run_with_limits with max_concurrent; spells out semaphore-token leaks and cleanup skipped when cancellation races a timeout. Same failure modes.
Async worker pool where a cancelled worker must release its connection and return its in-flight item; cancellation-safe resource release.
Async worker pool as a context manager with bounded concurrency and graceful shutdown; same primitives, class interface instead of a function.
Async scheduler with max_concurrent, dependencies and a shutdown deadline; adds dependency ordering on top of the same cancellation contract.
Async run_with_timeout over subprocesses with max_concurrent; bounded concurrency plus cancelling work that overruns.
A run_tasks in /app/run.py with max_workers and per-task timeouts, thread-based; same interface contract, different concurrency primitive.
Parallel executor with robust shutdown handling across worker processes; teaches shutdown ordering and not leaving orphans.

TMax-15K.reason: Background tasks are not cancelled or cleaned up when the connection closes; fix the lifecycle. Same cancellation-and-cleanup bug, fully pinned tests.

Proxy hangs and leaks when connections are abruptly cancelled; strong verifier and the same abrupt-cancellation cleanup question.
Implement a worker-pool pattern over asyncio.Queue to process targets concurrently — the bounded-concurrency half, written from scratch.
Identify and fix an async task leak so a disconnecting client does not strand work; cancellation propagation across a service boundary.
Service becomes unresponsive and leaks resources when jobs are cancelled; the resource-release-on-cancel discipline this task tests.
Verified explicitly on the property that cancelled requests do not leave anything behind and do not spin the CPU.
A test_cancellation binary crashes when the engine is cancelled right after startup — the same cancel-during-startup race, in C.

Cancel the remaining tasks when one raises, instead of letting gather leave them running; teaches gather's cancellation behaviour.

Silence the 'task was destroyed but it is pending' warning by awaiting cancellation properly — the symptom of skipping cleanup.
asyncio.Semaphore RuntimeError from binding the semaphore to the wrong loop; the same primitive this task must use correctly.
Run many jobs while capping how many run simultaneously, with processes; identical concurrency-cap requirement, different primitive.
Contrast gather, wait and TaskGroup — precisely the choice that determines whether cleanup runs on cancel. Only 1 of 28 tests pins anything.
Producer-consumer over asyncio.Queue with workers that must stop cleanly; bounded workers plus shutdown.
Restructure broken asyncio code so coroutines are actually scheduled; basic event-loop competence, nothing about cancellation.

Run shell commands with a configurable cap on how many go in parallel; the bounded-concurrency contract, but the suite is FREE.

Run checks serially then in parallel, including a timeout case; comparing sequential and concurrent execution with deadlines.

Parallel pipeline over generated integers with a helper library; fan-out only, nothing about cancelling or cleaning up.

notes: CalibForge has an entire cluster of bounded-concurrency-with-graceful-shutdown implement-from-spec tasks, one of which (software-engineering_20260507_172207_003) is essentially the same problem statement as this TB2.1 task, down to the file path and the semaphore-permit-leak requirement; they are also strongly verified. TMax contributes the other genuinely useful family: real asyncio task-leak-on-cancellation bugs in services, which train the same CancelledError reasoning from the debugging side. Terminal-Lego is the most on-topic corpus by text — it is the only pool with tasks literally about cleaning up an interrupted event loop and about asyncio concurrency limiters — but its verification is too thin for final_top10; if the merge wants keyword coverage of KeyboardInterrupt cleanup, task_10192 and task_10167 are the two to look at, with eyes open about their suites. TerminalWorld and Recursive-Task-Synthesis have no asyncio content at all; their entries are process-and-signal analogues and should be treated as filler below rank 3 or so.
